The first public release. A permanent GPU-accelerated desktop that exists to be tested in, so no experiment needs a production container or the host.

## ✨ Added

- A full [Selkies](https://github.com/selkies-project/selkies) desktop with the box's **GPU**, a real **Firefox** and a real **Google Chrome**, both opening real windows on `DISPLAY=:1`. Headful clicks, pointer lock, hardware decode and screenshots all need a desktop that actually draws.
- A **toolchain in the image**: Go, Node, Python, git, a C and C++ toolchain, and Playwright's operating-system dependencies. The browser binaries are deliberately skipped, since the system Firefox and Chrome cover that.
- **`/config` as the only persistent mount.** `GOPATH` and the npm global prefix live there, so a container rebuild keeps them. Nothing else is mounted, so the sandbox cannot reach production data: it was never handed a path to it.
- **An Unraid template** ([`templates/trialyard.xml`](templates/trialyard.xml)) with hard CPU and memory ceilings rather than reservations, on its own address so no port mapping is needed.
- **The image is published**, so it can be pulled rather than built:

  ```
  docker pull ghcr.io/junkerderprovinz/trialyard:latest
  ```

  `amd64` only: Google Chrome ships no arm64 Linux build, and the GPU this is built around is an x86_64 machine's.

## ⚡ Improved

- The desktop **says how to use itself**. The right-click menu was built correctly and was entirely undiscoverable, which from a browser is indistinguishable from a broken container. The wallpaper now names it, because a user cannot be expected to guess at black.
- The **hint fits any window**. Selkies resizes the desktop to whatever the browser window is, so the wallpaper is fitted rather than cropped and the leftover is filled with the same colour, instead of the sentence appearing twice side by side.

## Notes

No Community Applications listing and no Docker Hub mirror yet. The source is published so that its history lives somewhere other than a single folder on an array: an image built from a state nobody can reach again cannot be inspected later, only rebuilt from scratch.
